articleTitle: RAGLog: Log Anomaly Detection using Retrieval Augmented Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: The ability to detect log anomalies from system logs is a vital activity needed to ensure cyber resiliency of systems. It is applied for fault identification or facilitate cyber investigation and digital forensics. However, as logs belonging to different systems and components differ significantly, the challenge to perform such analysis is humanly challenging from the volume, variety and velocity of logs. This is further complicated by the lack or unavailability of anomalous log entries to develop trained machine learning or artificial intelligence models for such purposes. In this research work, we explore the use of a Retrieval Augmented Large Language Model that leverages a vector database to detect anomalies from logs. We used a Question and Answer configuration pipeline. To the best of our knowledge, our experiment which we called RAGLog is a novel one and the experimental results show much promise.

articleTitle: Situation Awareness-based Evacuation Assistance System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Evacuating buildings during various emergencies, such as fire or terrorist attacks, requires high awareness of the environment, quick decision-making, and immediate action. In recent years, the research has increased regarding how to support this process and persons involved by dedicated technical means. However, still, a lot of questions remain unanswered. This contribution presents a concept and the first mobile application design as part of an intuitive evacuation assistance system for evacuation leaders to improve emergency situation awareness of individual leaders and the evacuation team. Using the proposed system, the leaders will get real-time support regarding environmental hazards, evacuation procedures, extra assistance requests, the number of people in the building or their area, etc., improving the overall situation awareness. This can be achieved by a proper sensory infrastructure, intelligent algorithms building an artificial situation awareness, and a user-focused interface design, as introduced in this contribution.The analytical discussion presented in this contribution points out the strength of the concept, and the first tests of sensory infrastructure presented show feasibility for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Blueprinting Critical Infrastructure Coordination Centre
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: In recent years, critical infrastructures (CIs) have been subjected to sophisticated attacks (e.g., Stuxnet) leading to severe consequences. CIs are also exposed to natural hazards (earthquakes, flooding, etc.) capable of disrupting their operation. Cyber-physical attacks on CIs can lead to economic and socio-political consequences as well as cascading effects between them. As the nature of operations in EU’s internal market is progressively inter-connected and cross-border, several sectors and protective measures which go beyond individual CI are described in the Directive (EU) 2022/2557 on the resilience of critical entities (‘’CER Directive") adopted in 2022, Furthermore, the Directive (EU) 2022/2555 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union (‘’NIS 2 Directive") was also adopted. Therefore, Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) requires stakeholders to coordinate their actions in preventing and managing cyber-attacks on CIs. This paper presents a representation of a coordination center based on European recommendations and best practices to help standardize and facilitate the adaptation of coordination centers in CIP. This paper presents an Information System Architecture (InfoSA) and an Information Architecture (InfoA) of a Critical -Infrastructure Coordination Centre (3C) based on the outcomes of the PRECINCT (Preparedness and Resilience Enforcement for Critical INfrastructure Cascading Cyber-Physical Threats) project.

articleTitle: A LoRa-Powered Secure Vehicular Communication System: Internet of Vehicles (IoV)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: The implications of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) concept grow with the number and variety of connected vehicles. Safe transportation becomes important when vehicle users seek comfort on the road. Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication technology enhances communication between vehicles and infrastructure. To meet the growing demand for connected vehicles, network speed, energy efficiency, and spectrum consumption must be improved over ad-hoc or cellular connectivity. The current research utilizes Low-Power, Wide-Area Networking (LPWAN) technology as Long-Range (LoRa). Scalability, flexibility, long-range, and low power consumption are all provided by LoRa communication over the Long Range-Wide Area Network (LoRaWAN). The current work is a proof-of-concept for a hardware prototype on a Vehicular Ad- Hoc Network (VANET) that employs LoRa modules and a LoRaWAN gateway. The proposed system is tested for Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) and Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) communication between LoRa devices, and it sends data to a LoRaWAN server via the gateway. The test results significantly support the usefulness of the proposed method for establishing a secure connection in connected vehicles. The acquired metrics of the better-received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) and Signal Noise Ratio (SNR), support the proposed method for enhanced communication utilizing LoRaWAN for connected vehicles.

articleTitle: P-TimeSync: A Precise Time Synchronization Simulation with Network Propagation Delays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Time serves as the foundation of modern society and will continue to grow in value in the future world. Unlike previous research papers, authors delve into various time sources, ranging from atomic time and GPS time to quartz time. Specifically, we explore the time uncertainty associated with the four major Global Navigation Satellite Systems. In existing time synchronization simulations provide partial usages. However, our research introduces a comprehensive and precise time synchronization simulation named P-TimeSync, leading to a better understanding of time synchronization in distributed environments. It is a state-of-the-art simulation tool for time because (1) it can simulate atomic clocks and quartz clocks with user-defined software clock algorithms, (2) the simulation provides nanosecond-level precision time across different network propagation paths and distances, (3) the tool offers a visualization platform with classic algorithms for distributed time synchronization, such as Cristian’s algorithm and Berkeley algorithm. The simulation easily allows for the redefinition of configurations and functions, supporting advanced research and development. The simulation tool could be downloaded via the website: https://github.com/rui5097/purdue_timesync

articleTitle: Smart Soil Nutrient Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: In the dynamic realm of precision agriculture, the "Soil Nutrient Analyzer" stands tall as a groundbreaking project, revolutionizing how we approach crop cultivation. Leveraging the power of the NPK sensor, Arduino Nano, Modbus, and an OLED screen, this innovative system aims to decode the soil's nutritional secrets, thus assisting farmers in making informed decisions for optimal crop selection. The project's core functionality involves extracting Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium values directly from the soil, providing valuable insights into the soil's fertility.

articleTitle: AI-Powered Crisis Response: Streamlining Emergency Management with LLMs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Facing the urgent requirement for effective emergency management, our study introduces a groundbreaking approach leveraging the capabilities of open-source Large Language Models (LLMs), notably LLAMA2. This system is engineered to enhance public emergency assistance by swiftly processing and classifying emergencies communicated through social media and direct messaging. Our innovative model interprets user descriptions to analyze context and integrate it with existing Situation Reports, streamlining the alert process to government agencies with crucial information. Importantly, during peak emergency times when conventional systems are under stress, our LLM-based solution provides critical support by offering straightforward guidance to individuals and facilitating direct communication of their circumstances to emergency responders. This advancement significantly bolsters the efficiency and efficacy of crisis response mechanisms.

articleTitle: Leveraging Public Safety and Enhancing Crack Detection in Concrete Bridges using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: The safety of transportation networks is intrinsically linked to the reliability of their infrastructure. Throughout their life cycle, bridges are subject to numerous types of damage that are generally monitored using several Structural Health Monitoring methods. Cracks, the most common defect encountered in concrete bridges, have been the main focus of numerous research works investigating several frameworks based on computer vision for crack detection automation. This paper proposes a pixel-level crack detection method in concrete bridge surfaces leveraging the popular semantic segmentation model UNet and two benchmark public crack datasets. The results have demonstrated the efficiency of the proposed framework as the model achieved a mean Intersection over Union of 76.92% and an F1-Score of 70.45%. The trained model was further tested on two high-resolution images to detect cracks in complex and noisy concrete bridge surfaces, and the width of the cracks was estimated using image processing techniques. The results showcase the potential use of the segmentation outputs to analyze cracks and assess their severity level and impact on bridges' structural safety.

articleTitle: Distributed Acoustic Sensor System for Vehicle Occupancy Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: A distributed acoustic sensors (DAS) system is investigated in this paper to offer vehicle occupancy detection for intelligent transportation systems (ITS). Accurate detection of the number of occupants in a vehicle is critical for ITS to mitigate safety risks, including monitoring overloading behaviour and ensuring the legal use of high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lanes. Several deep learning (DL) algorithms have been designed to obtain occupancy by analyzing DAS signals. An AlexNet and a slim visual geometry group (SVGG) algorithm are designed to analyze the data of a single DAS sensor. Furthermore, a sparse residual network (SR-Net) is proposed to process merged signals collected by multiple DAS sensors. We collected DAS data in road experiments and tested the proposed DL approaches. The test results indicate that 1) both the proposed Alexnet and SR-Net approaches can achieve detection accuracy of over 90%; 2) the proposed SR-Net model exhibits superior convergence, stability, and accuracy than the conventional residual network (ResNet); 3) the proposed DL solutions have practical complexity and model size.

articleTitle: Proposed Components for the Information Architecture of a Critical Infrastructure Coordination Centre
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel model for the Information Architecture of a Critical Infrastructures Coordination Center, emphasizing its reliance on digital components such as metadata, procedural metadata, and smart contracts. The Information Architecture model represents an original approach to bolstering the resilience of infrastructures by addressing risk scenarios that are affected by cascading effects. The study approaches the problem of defining a business model for the Coordination Centers. The purpose is to identify the benefit-to-cost ratio of the Centers to provide evidence of the opportunity for investment in this solution. The Information Architecture is a component of the Enterprise Architecture introduced by NIST. The primary advantage of Enterprise Architecture is to provide stakeholders with a shared understanding of the needs and opportunities. Likewise, the Information Architecture abstraction presented here provides a simple framework for communicating the essential elements of interaction between critical infrastructure operators while maintaining a focus on trust as the key factor to promote cooperation to increase resilience.

articleTitle: Automated pill dispenser to improve medication compliance, efficiency, and accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Millions of people need to manually sort various medications into pill boxes, causing medication inaccuracies which is detrimental to public safety and an important cause of hospitalizations. It is especially challenging for seniors living alone and people with physical and mental disabilities to sort out pills and may need reminders to take their medications on time. There is an urgent need for a user-friendly home-based pill dispenser system to keep track of dosage and changes, in real-time, and dispense pills per schedule on time without the need to sort out pills in advance. Public safety personnel especially emergency response personnel who respond to medication overdoses and who temporally dispense medications during disaster relief, would benefit from having an automated pill dispenser device. There is currently no affordable, portable, and reliable automated pill dispensing and reminder device. A smart electronic pill dispenser was designed and 3D printed. An Arduino system and a custom-made Android application is used to electronically program a patient’s medication schedule. Two different pills are loaded into respective individual compartments. The android application guides the Arduino system to drop the individual pills into a receptacle below and an audio alarm alerts the patient to take the pills. The pill dispenser can accurately dispense medications without the need for manual sorting. In conclusion, the automated pill dispenser is a valuable device for use by patients and public safety personnel to be able to dispense medications conveniently and accurately.

articleTitle: Audio Simulation for Sound Source Localization in Virtual Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Non-line-of-sight localization in signal-deprived environments is a challenging yet pertinent problem. Acoustic methods in such predominantly indoor scenarios encounter difficulty due to the reverberant nature. In this study, we aim to locate sound sources to specific locations within a virtual environment by leveraging physically grounded sound propagation simulations and machine learning methods. This process attempts to overcome the issue of data insufficiency to localize sound sources to their location of occurrence especially in post-event localization. We achieve 0.786±0.0136 F1-score using an audio transformer spectrogram approach.

articleTitle: Connecting First Responders via a 5G Access-Agnostic Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: This paper explores the ability to connect heterogeneous first responders’ networks using a 5G core to provide resilient communications in mission-critical national security and public safety situations. The Non-3GPP Inter-Working Function (N3IWF) included in the 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) 5G Release 15 specification allows any access network to interface with a 5G network. In a lab testbed, the authors demonstrated a solution based on the 3GPP standards to allow non-3GPP devices to communicate through a 5G network to raise tactical awareness, report suspicious activities, and transport video footage of illegal movement of weapons, drugs, or people at the borders. Additionally, the testbed demonstrated the use of a 5G NAS-Proxy whose main function is to support the registration, mobility, and session management needed to establish and maintain Internet Protocol (IP) connectivity between a user equipment (UE) and a data network through a 5G core. The 5G NAS-Proxy allows legacy UEs that cannot be modified or upgraded to seamlessly access a data network using 5G core. The novelty of the solution shows that (1) 5G is access agnostic; (2) the N3IWF gateway allows first responders' tactical radios and the applications using these radios to securely connect to a 5G core network, and (3) the legacy UEs and their applications do not require any software upgrade or re-configuration to access the 5G network. This paper describes the design and requirements of the NAS-Proxy and future work will center on investigating the potential issues that might arise when using N3IWF with non-3GPP waveforms that do not support IP and determining the minimum access network performance parameters (data rate, latency etc.) necessary to establish and maintain connection to a 5G Core network.

articleTitle: Creating a shared public safety radio data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: We aim to gather Land Mobile Radio (LMR) data from a wide range of public safety organizations (PSOs) across the country. The primary objective is to conduct research and analysis to gain insights into the potential impacts of transitioning from LMR to LTE technology. Our team is collaborating with ten different PSOs nationwide, acquiring not only LMR data but also relevant geographical details, including weather and event information. These data sets will serve as resources for in-depth research and analysis, allowing us to better understand LMR usage patterns and to prepare for a successful transition to LTE.

articleTitle: Secure Information Discovery between Public Security Authorities Using a New Pseudonymization Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Secure information discovery between independent security authorities is a major challenge in times when crime organizations co-operate more and more across national borders. Isolated databases, security, and privacy regulations as well as a lack of trust often hinder an efficient information exchange between security authorities. E.g., national police authorities of the 27 Member States of the European Union (EU) must use a manual process to send separate secure emails to each other if they need to identify if a suspect is known to the other police authority. To overcome these obstacles a distributed semi-automated hit-/no hit-system for secure information discovery between federated organizations has been developed. This system uses a Bloom-filter based pseudonymization allowing for similarity searches between pseudonyms. The system has been tested in a pilot phase of the European Police Records Index System (EPRIS) which will become the basis for the new regulation for automated data exchange for police cooperation in the EU. This paper describes the approach and the preliminary results of the pilotphase.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on ODMRP for Police Ad hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Ad hoc network is a type of network built for some specific objectives and not depending on infrastructure. Multicast is important applications for Ad hoc network. ODMRP is a multicast routing protocol for Ad hoc network. It is characterized by simplicity, mesh route, and dynamic topology. However, a detailed simulation study on ODMRP is still missing. Based on OPNET, this article built the model library for ODMRP, including network model, node model, and process model, etc. A group of numerical simulations are done based on these models. Simulation results verify the validity of these models and quantitatively show that the performance of ODMRP decrease with the increase of node movement speed and multicast group size. The model library built by this article can provide ready-to-use services for academic researchers and industrial personnel.

articleTitle: Verifiable Credentials in US Government Disaster Relief
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: With increasingly damaging natural disasters, the US federal, state, and local governments face growing challenges to efficient and effective disaster relief. The relief and aid application process is often redundant with many organizations providing disaster relief assistance. Each organization often duplicates the process for identity and document verification. Individuals face barriers when applying for needed assistance due to the challenging and redundant identity and documentation verification processes. Individuals need an easier way to handle their disaster relief applications to reduce complexity of securing necessary aid. Government organizations have an opportunity to reduce the work required to process relief applications and improve the interoperability between organizations vetting individuals’ documents. In this poster, we present a future disaster relief system that lowers the barrier of application for disaster relief for applicants and reduces redundant operations by both government service providers and individual applicants by using verifiable credentials. Using an initial use case of tropical storm disasters, we present this future system for community feedback during the poster session and to aid our goal to increase community and individual safety through expedited disaster relief distributions and improved recovery.

articleTitle: Classification of Indicator of Compromise for physics-based attacks in quantum communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Quantum communications are based on the law of physics for information security and the implications for this form of future information security enabled by quantum science has to be studied. Physics-based vulnerabilities may exist due to the inherent physics properties and behavior of quantum technologies such as Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), thus resulting in new threats that may emerge with attackers exploiting the physics-based vulnerabilities. There were many studies and experiments done to demonstrate the threat of physics-based attacks on quantum links. However, there is a lack of a framework that provides a common language to communicate about the threats and type of adversaries being dealt with for physics-based attacks. This work is a review of physics-based attacks that were being investigated and attempt to initialize a framework based on the attack objectives and methodologies, pioneering the classification of Indicator of Compromises (IoCs) for physics-based attacks. This work will also pave the way for future work in the development of a forensic tool for the different classification of IoCs, with the methods of evidence collections and possible points of extractions for analysis being further investigated.

articleTitle: Decentralized Drug Transaction Tracking: A Novel Hybrid Blockchain-IPFS Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Counterfeit drugs are a serious global problem that poses threats to public health. It occurs when falsified or counterfeit drugs are intentionally manufactured and introduced into the pharmaceutical supply chain, masquerading as genuine products. This is due to the complexity of the supply chain that involves independent entities. As a result, a drug transits through several stages before reaching the patient. Current drug management systems are centralized, thus creating data transparency and authenticity risks within the supply chain. To bypass this issue, we propose in this paper a novel hybrid and distributed drug transaction tracking platform that leverages a combination of the Interplanetary File System (IPFS) protocol and Ethereum blockchain. Relying on IPFS guarantees the integrity of drug traceability data, while the blockchain ensures the authenticity of this data. We developed our platform and, through experiments, we prove that our method is more efficient, in terms of process costs, than the conventional blockchain-based drug tracking system.

articleTitle: Automated Transformer Bund Wall Drainage System to Mitigate Climate Change Risks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: In the age of the digital transformation and all the potential benefits and modernized proposals that it promises, it is important for power utilities to begin implementation of these proposed benefits rather than wait for a ‘step-change’ that may never come. To clarify this, an automated transformer bund wall drainage system has been proposed in this paper. This system would replace the manual intervention that is presently required to periodically drain the transformer bund of accumulated rainwater. The proposed Internet of Things (IoT) based system would be required to autonomously detect the level of rainwater, drain it when required to ensure adequate containment of transformer oil in the event of a leak and also to ensure that transformer oil would not release into the environment. With the anticipated increase in precipitation due to climate change this system would eliminate the increased environmental risk and also save maintenance costs by reducing the need for human intervention and labour.

articleTitle: ActionPoint: An App to Combat Cyberbullying by Strengthening Parent-Teen Relationships
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Due to the increased prevalence of cyberbullying and the detrimental impact it can have on adolescents, there is a critical need for tools to help combat cyberbullying. This paper introduces the ActionPoint app, a mobile application based on empirical work highlighting the importance of strong parent-teen relationships for reducing cyberbullying risk. The app is designed to help families improve their communication skills, set healthy boundaries for social media use, identify instances of cyberbullying and cyberbullying risk, and, ultimately, decrease the negative outcomes associated with cyberbullying. The app guides parents and teens through a series of interactive modules that engage them in evidence-based activities that promote better understanding of cyberbullying risks and healthy online behaviors. In this paper, we describe the app design, the psychology research supporting the design of each module, the architecture and implementation details, and crucial paths to extend the app.

articleTitle: Drones Optimization for Public Transportation Safety: Enhancing Surveillance and Efficiency in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: In the context of smart cities, the adoption of multi-UAV systems has become a key focus in enhancing traffic management, particularly to fortify public safety. This study addresses the challenge of optimizing traffic management through the application of swarm-based Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). The research strategically aims to minimize the number of deployed drones for monitoring extensive road networks, fostering cost-efficiency within smart city contexts. Our investigation introduces a mathematical model, the swarm-drone set covering problem, to optimize coverage. Through a detailed computational experiment, we showcase the effectiveness of the algorithm in minimizing deployment while maintaining surveillance efficiency. Notably, our results reveal a significant correlation: as the radius of coverage for individual UAVs increases, the required number of UAVs decreases, underscoring the impact of coverage radius on resource optimization. The findings of this study contribute to the advancement of safety, security, and overall transportation network management in smart cities.

articleTitle: Smart Communities, Smart Responders -Artificial Intelligence for Internet of Things Competition: A Case Study in Organizing a Public Safety Innovation Challenge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: The rollout of 5G infrastructure, the proliferation of devices in the Internet of Things, and the integration of innovative technologies into buildings, transportation, and public safety systems have brought many benefits to communities throughout the country. However, this has also created a large amount of data, making it difficult for public safety leaders and first responders to use it. To address one aspect of this issue, the Smart Communities, Smart Responders: An Artificial Intelligence for Internet of Things Prize Competition was established. The main goal of this initiative is to accelerate the development of real-time data analysis and visualization, facilitated by the integration of sensors, allowing access to a variety of IoT data streams in user-friendly formats. This will give first responders the ability to tackle complex problems by combining and integrating sensor data, thus improving situational analysis and response times. Texas A&M University, Texas A&M Engineering Extension Service, and US-Ignite invited the public to participate in the competition, which is funded by the National Institute of Standards and Technology Public Safety Communications Research Division. Contestants are challenged to ingest unfamiliar data, assess them based on metadata or contextual cues using machine learning methods, and classify them for use on a situational awareness platform. The competition was organized in three phases over the course of 12 months. The selected contestants from the previous phases were given the opportunity to develop their solutions, preparing and participating in a live testing event hosted at Disaster City® managed by Texas A&M Engineering Extension Service.

articleTitle: Jamming Attacks on FSO Networks: Challenges, Opportunities, and a Public Safety Use-Case
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Among the candidate sixth-generation (6G) enabling technologies, free-space optical (FSO) technology has the potential to deliver high-performance thanks to its high throughput data links due to its unlicensed spectrum and wide bandwidth. However, FSO communication is adversely affected by fading caused by inherent channel anomalies. Along with these channel impairments, fabricated adversaries, such as jamming attacks, are also possible in FSO-based networks. Jammers threaten a security-constrained application, such as surveillance systems, to monitor critical areas where extra-trustworthy communication is required. This paper provides an overview of the vital issue of jamming attacks on FSO-based networks. It offers essential pointers to interested readers and future researchers on open research issues in this area. It also discusses the critical challenges related to existing security measures against jamming attacks in FSO-based networks. In addition, this paper presents a use-case scenario that evaluates the spectral efficiency performance of an FSO-based vehicular network under a jamming attack.

articleTitle: AIM: Using AI to Improve Residential Racial and Economic Segregation for Mortality Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Residential racial and economic segregation has been associated with an increased risk for main causes of death. Quintiles of the Index of Concentration and the Extremes (ICE) are commonly used to measure residential segregation because of their robust and comprehensiveness. However, the high correlation between ICE and the proportion of population in poverty can cause the collinearity, and this issue was avoided by ignoring poverty rate or transforming the continuous variable to the category variable in previous research, which induced the missing information because poverty was one significantly crucial covariant in different models for the association of residential segregation and health outcomes. In this paper we developed one new methodology named AIM by exploring artificial intelligence (AI) techniques to extract the integrated information from poverty. The original algorithm of this methodology utilized the high correlation between ICE and poverty rate to implement balanced clustering, by which ICE quintiles were improved and the stronger association of the AI based segregation with age-adjusted mortality rate was observed.

articleTitle: Change Address Detection in Bitcoin using Hierarchical Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: The widespread adoption and success of blockchain, particularly Bitcoin, was influenced by the promise of decentralization and anonymity. Sadly, these same characteristics have made it attractive to illegal activities, requiring careful oversight and targeted interventions. In order to mitigate illicit usage of this technology, we need to analyze and de-anonymize transactions occurring in the blockchain. For that purpose, change addresses identification is a promising technique, since change addresses can be associated to the inputs of the same transaction since they are meant to hold leftover funds for the same user. In this article, we propose a new approach of change address detection using hierarchical clustering. First, we developed a new method for data extraction of connected transactions. After collecting the transaction, we combined multiple input heuristics with a hierarchical clustering algorithm at the transaction level to study similarities in usage patterns between inputs and outputs. After applying our detection model, we analyze the generating cluster and evaluate the performance of our solution in terms of F1-score, result accuracy, recall and precision.

articleTitle: Deep Recurrent Neural Networks for Highway Traffic Flow Prediction at Toll Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Intelligent transportation systems have gained a significant momentum in recent years due to the advancements in computing hardware, sensors and related infrastructure. A key component of the aforementioned systems is traffic flow prediction; that is, the ability to forecast the evolution of traffic volume in future time windows, either short-term or long-term. Benefits of traffic flow forecasting on city, regional, trans-regional roads and highways include the ability of drivers to better plan their journey in order to avoid traffic congestion, the capability of regulation authorities to apply proactive policies such as diverting traffic to alternative routes so as to avoid foreseen bottlenecks or even the option of highway concessionaires to adjust their tariff policies based on the predictive volume of traffic. In this work, a novel traffic flow prediction system, based on deep recurrent neural networks, that has been developed from scratch, is presented. The proposed system is trained on traffic data collected at the entrance toll stations of Olympia Odos, a major highway in Greece, and is subsequently deployed to the infrastructure of Olympia Odos S.A, the concessionaire of the highway, with predictions being publicly available via a web interface and mobile applications. The overall architecture exhibits more than satisfactory performance both in normal traffic conditions and in cases of increased traffic (weekends, public holidays etc).

articleTitle: Leveraging Commercial Connected Vehicle Data for High-Speed Signalized Intersection Safety: A Quantitative Analysis of Hard-Braking and Crashes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: This study leverages commercial connected vehicle (CCV) data to address road safety issues at high-speed signalized intersections in Iowa. The study focuses on assessing road safety using minimal CCV data. The temporal stability analysis of the data concluded that the 8-week data was relatively stable. By testing the correlation between the number of hard braking at different intersections and crash data in 8 weeks of randomly selected CCV data, it was concluded that hard braking and crashes have a high correlation (greater than 0.5). Additionally, the study explores the predictive power of CCV data on crash risk and time distribution throughout the day. The results reflect the importance of real-time insights from CCV data for targeted interventions, highlighting the need for a data-driven approach to enhance overall road safety.

articleTitle: Public Safety Campus Networks: Towards a Reference Architecture for Post-Disaster Edge-Computing and Crisis-Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: The impact of disasters on communication infrastructure can have dramatic consequences for citizens. To ensure their safety, it is important to keep as many citizens as possible in disaster areas connected to emergency-communication and public safety services especially when home-based communication and mobile-network infrastructure failed. This work presents a proposal towards a reference-architecture for edge-computing with Public Safety Campus Networks (PSCN) deployed in disaster-stricken areas. Mobile phones within coverage of these networks may automatically attach with the network and thus provide citizens with post-disaster communication over cellular network. Based on a standards-driven approach, our proposal integrates the 5G Core, Multi-Access Edge-Computing (MEC) and edge-hosted public safety services for bi-directional post-disaster communication into a unified reference-architecture. This work further presents a study on the transformation of a public warning/alerting system, currently deployed in Germany, transforming its architecture from a centralized towards an edge-enabled architecture, making it deployable in Public Safety Campus Networks.

articleTitle: Building Occupancy Estimation Using Multilayer Perceptron
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: The recent advancements in the Internet of Things have facilitated the deployment of efficient and cost-effective sensors in buildings which allows the collection of comprehensive environment data that can be used for machine learning training and prediction of occupancy status. Deep learning models such as multilayer perceptron can be used to predict the occupancy information from environmental sensor data for various applications including smart environment and security. Due to privacy concerns, environmental sensing data collection is less intrusive and preferred in areas such as homes, offices, or similar environments. They can be safely released as public datasets and researchers can use them for their study without the need to create their own test beds to collect data. This work presents a machine-learning application for building occupancy count estimation using environmental sensor data from multiple homes. Multilayer perceptron training is performed on a publicly available real-world dataset containing comprehensive non-invasive sensor data and the occupied status and occupancy count estimation is performed with a high accuracy.

articleTitle: Navigating Change: Enhancing Transportation Resilience in the Face of Climate Change - A Moroccan Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Climate change manifested through extreme weather events such as hurricanes, floods, wildfires, and rising sea levels, poses significant threats to transportation infrastructure, disrupts services, and raises safety concerns with dangerous repercussions on the broader economic sector. Drawing insights from the Moroccan Ministry of Equipment and Water on climate change and resilience, we delve into the unique challenges and vulnerabilities faced by the transportation sector in Morocco amidst a changing climate. The study explores advanced technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI) and computer vision, to mitigate the impacts of climate change on transportation safety. Emphasizing the need for foresighted measures, we explore applications such as computer vision for weather pattern recognition by analyzing satellite imagery and real-time monitoring via video feeds. This approach enables accurate and timely predictions of extreme weather events, facilitating improved preparedness and response strategies. The findings contribute to the broader discourse on climate change adaptation and sustainable development, offering a nuanced perspective based on the specific realities of the Moroccan transportation scene.

articleTitle: A Systems Approach to CSI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Forensic science is the core of crime scene investigations (CSI), a niche mastered by few experts world-wide. Crime scene investigators skillfully determine the most suitable sequence of methods for valuable evidence recovery from crime scenes, e.g., blood trace detection and blood-stained footmark or fingermark recovery. This professionalism demands a high degree of experience, memory, judgment, and decision making. Digital aids for such tasks are still scarce, whereas checklists and diagrams are heavily used. We propose an original systems approach to CSI, coupled with a Digital Companion for Crime Scene Investigation (DC4CSI) – a model-based digital engineering (MBDE) proof of concept. We introduce a model-based, unified, end-to-end, layered socio-technical architecture (people, technology, and processes etc.) for CSI. We incorporate forensic expert support through method execution and integration with physical environments and devices. Our method uses OPCloud, an emerging digital platform capable of expressing, exhibiting, and executing any type of system using Object Process Methodology (OPM) – a holistic systems modeling paradigm. The results of our approach include: a) a common language for CSIs and other crime-scene engaging parties, b) reduced checklists-based traditional work, and c) enhanced decision automation for effective and efficient evidence recovery.

articleTitle: Federated cloud-native service placement in latency-sensitive and resource-constrained scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: This paper constitutes the contribution on the 5G-EPICENTRE service placement module. The module is a part of the federation layer and determines the best cluster for service deployment, where "best" is defined as the one contributing better to make an efficient (load balanced) use of computing resources, whilst fulfilling the stringent service requirements in terms of latency. In this direction, this paper presents a comprehensive solution to address the critical challenges associated with service management and resource allocation in emergency scenarios. This was achieved through the design and development of a built-in module, specifically for managing services based on their requirements in emergency situations. Our module ensures that services are deployed optimally, even under stringent emergency conditions. This paper introduces the context of the problem, formulates it, and evaluates it under a variety of conditions, including varying loads and cluster capacities, number of clusters, service requirements, or other parameters, more related with the algorithm design itself, such as number of services per service batch (i.e., number of services being deployed simultaneously in the emergency scenario).

articleTitle: Towards System Level Simulations of Public Safety Applications over 5G NR Sidelink
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: The New Radio (NR) sidelink (SL) interface was initially specified to support NR Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) applications and lately to support NR Proximity Services (ProSe) public safety applications. Network support requirements differ between the operational demands of these two types of applications. Building upon an existing ns-3 NR V2X simulator, this paper details the extensions made to the simulator to cater to NR ProSe public safety applications. We use as case study the Mission Critical Push-to-Talk (MCPTT) application, a keystone of group communication in 5G NR public safety networks. We demonstrate through simulation results that our enhancements are essential for a more accurate representation of public safety applications.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Road Object Detection for Collision Avoidance in Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: With the population in metro cities rising, traffic congestion has become a significant issue, resulting in an alarming number of traffic collisions and road accidents. Given the advancements in automated vehicles, it is crucial to have a vehicle detection system that is equipped to handle the various challenges that arise on the road, particularly when it comes to traffic collisions. Although many datasets are available to support object detection for traffic monitoring and management, the suitability of these datasets for specific weather conditions across the globe needs to be analyzed. We present Canadian vehicle datasets (CVD) and analyze the YOLOv8-based deep learning model using CVD. Thales, Canada, captured street-level videos in Quebec City, Canada, with a vehicle equipped with a high-quality RGB camera. The videos are taken day and night in all four seasons: rain, snow, hazy, and bright sunlight. We created 27378 labels for 11 classes for 8000 images. The YOLOv8 model trained on the publicly available roboFlow dataset was compared to the model trained on the combined roboflow and our weather-specific CVD.

articleTitle: How Trustworthy are Over-The-Air (OTA) Updates for Autonomous Vehicles (AV) to Ensure Public Safety?: A Threat Model-based Security Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: The rise of autonomous vehicles (AV) has transformed our transportation sectors in recent years. The evolution of technology has made AVs more popular among users. The Over-The-Air (OTA) updates for AVs are widely adopted by the AV industry. These updates are used to deliver improved functionality and security patches to ensure public safety. However, this system is susceptible to security threats since the wireless communication link between the car, the manufacturer, and the cloud-based web server is inherently insecure. While there are studies that explored multiple cybersecurity frameworks and tools for OTA updates, many challenges remain unaddressed. To build a robust trustworthy system, we need to perform a thorough security analysis by creating a threat model. In this study, we use the CIAA and STRIDE threat modeling process to analyze the OTA updates security. Our analysis demonstrates numerous dangers and vulnerabilities. To increase the security of OTA updates, we also suggest several corrective mitigation steps.

articleTitle: Security Analysis of Connected Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs): Challenges, Issues, Defenses, and Open Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: Our world is evolving into a landscape of smart cities, with connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) occupying a central role in the paradigm of smart mobility. To ensure road and public safety, transportation productivity, employment opportunities, and cost-effectiveness, the CAVs can be the pioneers in the overall transportation system. Renowned automobile companies are transforming and expanding their market into CAVs as future cars by creating additional AV wings in their industries. However, having modern technologies, these cars face unique challenges in operation and can be intended to be attacked by malicious entities. In this survey paper, we classified the attacks in terms of issues arising into three sectors of autonomous vehicles (AVs) – AV forensics, AV communications, and OTA updates for AV. We emphasize the security analysis by discussing several challenges, attack scenarios and defenses, and a few open problems. We anticipate that our paper will serve as a valuable resource for readers and apprentices working on attacks and defenses on connected autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Sustainable Flood Risk Identification and Assessment Using Artificial Intelligence: A Literature Review and Case Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: The combination of Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been widely applied in various fields, including transportation, agriculture, tourism, smart cities, environmental monitoring, and security. The growing accessibility of satellite and drone imagery, as well as remote sensing data, such as drones, has enabled the efficient utilization and training of deep learning algorithms. These algorithms can accurately identify, categorize, and partition flood areas in real-time. By integrating artificial intelligence (Al)-powered flood detection algorithms with additional data sources, such as meteorological forecasts and ground-based sensors, it is possible to create robust flood monitoring systems. These systems can offer timely alerts for potential flood events and enable efficient emergency response measures. The paper outlines advanced functionalities and technologies that will be available by integrating the Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) for flood monitoring. The paper provides a comprehensive overview of AI-IoT visions, services, applications, and the networking infrastructure involved. Additionally, it includes a vast assortment of satellite images.

articleTitle: Towards an Automated Cybersecurity Risk Assessment of Next Generation Emergency Communication Networks - NG911
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: The main objective of Next Generation Emergency Communication system in North America (NG911) is to enable reliable, more efficient assistance and quicker response times for first responders. NG911 provides significant enhancements over previous systems by enabling multimedia communication (text, images, and video) and improved geolocation technology, allowing for precise real-time location identification. Developing a proper understanding and analysis of cybersecurity risks that can impact NG911 systems’ availability, integrity, and confidentiality is critical. This paper focuses on establishing a systematic approach to NG911 risk assessments informed by the ever-changing threat landscape, including current and emerging threats. We proposes a framework that leverages existing tools and processes to facilitate automated risk assessments tailored explicitly to NG911 services.

articleTitle: Human-Factor focused Application of STPA to Remotely driven Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the safety aspects of a Remote Driving System (RDS) using the System-Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA) methodology. The focus is on the human Remote Driver (RD) within the RDS, considering losses and system-level hazards associated with the human-in-the-loop scenario which focuses on the RD actions related to the change in Steering Wheel Angle (SWA). The STPA methodology is applied to identify Unsafe Control Actions (UCA) related to the change in SWA command, resulting in the identification of numerous Causal Factors (CF) that may lead to hazardous scenarios. Several UCAs and CFs are identified that provide information on potential hazards and risks associated with remote driving technology. Based on a selected UCA where the RD does not change the SWA when the road network requires lateral movement, 25 potential loss scenarios were identified and presented in this paper. The results of this work can contribute to the understanding of potential risks and the development of safety mitigation measures in the context of RDS which need to be validated in further research.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual FedAux-based Harvested Energy Prediction for Road Safety Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology (WFPST)
abstract: In the evolving landscape of road safety, the role of solar-powered Internet-of-Things (IoT) devices, crucial for supporting connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs) with enhanced computing and storage capabilities, is increasingly significant These devices, often deployed in remote areas such as transcontinental highways, rely heavily on their energy harvesting capabilities for optimal operation. Given their expected widespread deployment, this paper explores the challenge of accurately predicting harvested energy in such IoT devices. To do so, we introduce "Dual FedAux", a novel approach that blends Federated Learning with a dual-model architecture, integrating long short-term memory (LSTM) and Transformer models. This combination, which is enhanced with meta-learning, i.e., stacking ensemble learning, is particularly adapted for time series analysis, such as for energy prediction. Through experiments, we demonstrate that the proposed Dual FedAux significantly outperforms benchmark models in terms of root-mean-square error (RMSE) and convergence, thus underscoring its potential to enhance the efficiency and reliability of large-scale road safety IoT-based systems.
